ios.desc:
Sudoku, Nonogram, Kakuro, Slitherlink, Hashi and Masyu: 68 puzzle types in one ad-free collection. Start with a favorite, then discover your next challenge.

Find your kind of puzzle
- Enjoy number puzzles? Try Sudoku, Calcudoku and Futoshiki.
- Follow number clues in Slitherlink, draw a single loop through the black and white pearls in Masyu, or connect islands in Hashi.
- Shade and divide grids in Nonogram, Nurikabe and Shikaku.
- Try something different with Minesweeper, Tents and Trees, or Star Battle.

Learn by playing
Interactive tutorials let you practice unfamiliar rules on the board. Choose from each game's available sizes and difficulties, and play practice puzzles offline at your own pace. New boards are generated so you can keep exploring.

Start free, explore more with Pro
Generate and play new boards free in 51 game types. The other 17 Pro games each include 5 different free boards, shared across practice and challenges. Pro unlocks unlimited new boards in those games, plus full replay history, advanced replay controls and long-term statistics.

Make time for a puzzle
Take on the shared daily challenge, review real games in replays, or follow your progress. Online challenges, rankings and cloud features need an internet connection.

Included puzzles:
Numbers & symbols: Sudoku, Calcudoku, Kakuro, Futoshiki, Binairo, Binairo+, Mathrax, Skyscrapers, Hidoku, ABCD, ABC End View, Hitori, Subsets
Loops & connections: Slitherlink, Masyu, Hashi, Yajilin, Shingoki, Gokigen Naname, Spokes, Train Tracks, Signpost, NetWalk, Netslide, Roma, Stitches
Shading & regions: Nonogram, Mosaic, Nurikabe, Fillomino, Shikaku, Heyawake, LITS, Norinori, Tapa, Shakashaka, Kurodoko, Palisade, Spiral Galaxies, Map, Yin-Yang
Placement & clues: Minesweeper, Battleships, Tents and Trees, Akari, Star Battle, Aquarium, Thermometers, Magnets, Kakurasu, Lollipops, Tatebo-Yokobo, Dominosa, Tawamurenga, Black Box, Haunted Mirror Maze, Mastermind
Movement & space: 15 Puzzle, Sixteen, Twiddle, Cube, Flip, Flood, SameGame, Inertia, Peg Solitaire, Planarity, Clusters

quotes.story_title: Ask HN: Share your personal website

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I’ve always loved Simon Tatham’s puzzle collection — especially Bridges, Slitherlink, and Signpost. I’ve been playing them for years on desktop and Android.

Recently I decided to port the collection to iOS with a more modern native UI and some usability improvements, while keeping the original puzzle generation logic intact.

The core puzzle engines are still Simon’s original C implementations. I built a thin Swift layer around them and focused mostly on:

Native SwiftUI interface

Better touch interactions

Dark mode

Offline support

Fast puzzle generation

Clean, minimal UI (no ads)

A few technical notes:

The puzzle logic runs as compiled C modules bridged into Swift

Puzzle state is serialized/deserialized to allow undo/redo

I implemented a custom rendering layer to support dynamic grid scaling

All puzzles are generated locally (no backend)

One thing I found interesting is how well the original C codebase is structured — it’s surprisingly modular for something that supports so many puzzle types.

I tried to stay faithful to the original mechanics while improving the mobile UX.

Would love feedback, especially from anyone familiar with the original project or who has thoughts on puzzle UI design.

App link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/simon-puzzles/id6756353841

Thanks Simon for building such a timeless collection.
